feedback.problem: Consider the standard basis ${i,j}$ of $\,{R}^{2}.$ If $T$ is a linear transformation such that $T(i)=i$ and $T(j)=2j,$ then what is the geometric interpretation of the transformation $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's consider the unit square spanned by the vectors $\,i\,$ and  $\,j.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/34c82826da26290fc890671734c354fbfd9c253f1cfaca38de1ea615434e6766.png)

Now, using the fact that $T(i)=i$ and $T(j)=2j,$ we can draw the image of the square under the transformation $T:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/56a5f95d469cb63e20936a6c07971d9e80611d966282cb37d7ddf17fdc761bab.png)

Therefore, the linear transformation $T$ represents a stretch with a scale factor $2$ in the $y$-direction.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: A stretch with a scale factor $2$ in the $y$-direction
